claim: Method and limits: every one of 1,785 reviews read in 18 batches in the original language (machine translation as a reading aid for zh/ja/ko/ru/tr/pl/bg, every quoted translation checked), hand codes with a quoted note per line, per-batch ID re-assertion caught three alignment drifts affecting 25 reviews; 166 codes, 25 unions, 636 checks, 8,300 computed facts, no number typed by hand; no duplicates, zero repeat authors, 60 edited, 254 with votes (max 82); the corpus is front-loaded — 645 reviews from 2016, 45.32% in E1 — so any global percentage is mostly a statement about 2016–17 ('Part 7 is not optional reading'); reviews decayed 59.1/month in E1 → 1.7/month in E5 (E5 59, E6 13 — directional only); no version field (Apple's history back to Mar 2020 only); 22 China-storefront reviews in English; six of 70 storefronts ≥50. Bands (verbatim): Share of reviews | Label ; < 0.1% | Ignore by default ; 0.1% – < 0.5% | Weak signal ; 0.5% – < 1% | Emerging signal ; 1% – < 3% | Meaningful signal ; 3% – 5% | Very strong signal ; > 5% | High-priority signal — 0.1% ≈ 2, 5% ≈ 89.

This corpus is not the app's rating: corpus 3.97★ vs every public storefront mean 4.5–4.8★ — 'written reviews here skew far more negative than silent star taps'; selection runs both ways (the 2016 launch wave and the 2022 black-screen wave are both bursts of motivated writers); 188 reviewers state they paid — a self-selected 10.53%, not a conversion rate.

The product's differentiator is visual and it worked for ten years: PR_DESIGN 460 (25.77%, 4.33★, 2016 → 2026), the single largest theme; with the per-habit cover photo (PR_PHOTOS 97, 5.43%) the visual union is 523 (29.30%, 4.36★); reviewers treat it as the mechanism, not decoration — 'I'm a very visual person, so the combination of large pictures and colourful calendars/graphs is great. I really feel motivated to tick things off, more than any other habit app' (4★); custom backgrounds named as the one reason productivity improved most across 15 trackers in three years; 'It sets a craving, when I see the image, I want to accomplish the goal'; paired with simplicity (PR_SIMPLE 361, 20.22%, 4.68★) this is what 'best in category' rests on — PR_BEST 204 (11.43%), 4.78★, the highest mean of any large theme.
this_app_does: full-screen photo per habit; free stock covers, paid custom

claim: The visual model — beauty is functional for a habit app because it makes you want to open it: 'because the design is beautiful, motivation rises easily — a surprisingly important point' (jp 4★); 'So beautiful that it makes me want to just do the items so I can click them off'; 'if it isn't all there in front of me in an endearing way, then I slack off and say NOPE'; 'It changes habit tracking from a chore into a fun experience I enjoy and look forward to'; a Good Design Award recipient in broadcast graphics: 'one of the most thoughtfully designed apps I have used' (2026).

Simplicity is defined negatively — the absence of what rivals do: 'No frills, no fuss—no need to sit through way-too-long animations and stories and celebrations every time you do something' (4★); 'a check-in app doesn't need lots of frills; this is just right' (cn); 'It doesn't give you confetti or a cookie but it helps form that path in your brain'; 'Perfect app. Don't ruin it with clutter!'.

Best-in-category and the named competition: PR_BEST 204 (11.43%, 4.78★ — the highest of any theme above 100); CMP_NAMED 48 (2.69%) — Way of Life, Momentum, Coach.me, Streaks, Done, Productive (2016), HabitBull, Habity, Shanbay (2017), iBetter, tiny routine, Strides (2018), Due (2019), Todoist, Day One, Evernote, Headspace, Notion (2022); Apple's Reminders, Calendar, Health and Activity named as both the thing replaced and the fallback; the corpus's most-voted review (38 up / 82): 'blew Momentum, Strides, and Way of Life out of the water… Momentum is too minimalistic (though I like their desktop sync, wink!) and Strides has a bubbly interface I can't stand' (2018).

claim: §8.4 immediate fix — never lose data, and never lose it from a paid backup: 12 of 55 data-loss reviewers had paid and backup is the paid feature (a wiped three-year history; a backup overwritten by the restore flow; 'lost ALL my information on 2 occasions'); minimum bar: restore must never destroy the backup it is reading, a failed restore must leave existing data intact, covers/photos must survive a restore; the right shape is probably optional account-based sync — not mandatory, because on-device data is something reviewers actively praise.

§8.5 immediate fix — ship the iOS home-screen widget: REQ_WIDGET 47, the only request that grows as the corpus shrinks (1.98% → 16.95%), home-screen requests 2020-09 → 2025-12; conversion evidence is unusually direct — 'they urgently need a widget and I swear I'd pay premium'; 'its lack of a widget means I'll probably need to look for something else'; the NC widget's history proves the value: the primary interface when it existed (PR_WIDGET 28, 4.50★), 11 complaints in six languages when it vanished for two months.
